changelog: Replace E1 with measured example en_us_738 to teach the model about negation + quantifier scope that resolves polarity and should not be cut.
Replace E2 with measured example en_us_936 to teach the model about conditional/subordinating scope ('Unless') that resolves truth conditions.
Replace E3 with measured example en_us_1116 to teach the model about exception clauses ('except') that reverse or limit prior claims.
Replace E4 with measured example en_us_103 to teach the model about numeral+unit and measurement phrases that determine scope and must stay attached.
findings: The prompt treats cuts before scope-resolving complements as acceptable: it allows a cut where the following phrase (exception, negation-resolver, quantifier/comparative, measurement phrase) determines or reverses the truth or scope of the already-delivered stretch.

The prompt often permits cuts that split a verb/copying auxiliary or copula from its essential complement (object, predicate adjective, prepositional/cause/contrast clause), breaking the proposition and harming cohesion.

diagnosis.why: Replacing the examples with negation/Unless/except/measurement cases taught the model to avoid cutting around scope-bearing tokens (negators, subordinators, exception markers and measurement phrases). That made it keep longer multiword constituents intact (small net gain on very long pieces, ≤99:+0.008) but pushed cuts into nearby short spans, producing small harms in the short-latency bins (≤3..≤10 negative) and slightly more (741) worsened than 690 improved pairs.
diagnosis.lesson: Respect scope-bearing attachments (negation, subordinators, exceptions, measurement phrases) but do so without shifting cuts so they split adjacent short constituents or verb phrases.
